b2-73.title: The marketing team
b2-73.story: Anna started a summer internship with the [[marketing]] team at a small juice company. On Monday, the [[product manager]] explained that they were launching a new mango drink. Anna's first job was to help write a [[press release]] for local news websites. Max, who works part-time as a concert [[promoter]], gave her some tips on getting people's attention. The team also planned a weekend [[promotion]]: buy one bottle and get the second one free. Anna designed a colorful [[flyer]] that students could hand out near the university. Meanwhile, the [[email marketing]] campaign reached thousands of customers at once. On Friday, Anna saw the mango drink on a huge [[billboard]] by the highway and sent a proud photo to her mama.

b2-74.title: Import and export
b2-74.story: Anna's dad works for a small company that sells Ukrainian honey abroad. Honey has become an important [[export]] for their region in the last few years. Last month, a large [[cargo]] of honey jars left Odesa by ship. A [[distributor]] in Poland agreed to deliver the jars to stores across the country. One big [[retailer]] even wanted to sell the honey on its website. At dinner, Taras asked why oil is sold by the [[barrel]] but honey isn't. Dad laughed and explained that oil [[trading]] works very differently from selling food. He also mentioned that the company's new delivery truck was an [[import]] from Germany. He had found it at an [[auction]] for half the usual price. Grandpa said the whole family should be proud, and Taras immediately asked for a free jar.

b2-75.title: A record year
b2-75.story: It was a record year for Lisa's family, and everyone wanted to celebrate. Her mom worked as the [[art director]] on a small Ukrainian comedy film. Surprisingly, the movie did really well at the [[box office]] all summer. Her dad, an [[economist]], wrote a simple book about saving money for teenagers. To his surprise, it became a [[bestseller]] in just three months. In the fall, he was invited to talk about it at a big book [[expo]] in Lviv. Even Lisa had good news: she remembered fifty digits of [[pi]] and won the school math contest. At the party, Anna joked that the family would soon need a bigger shelf for all their prizes.

b2-76.title: Banking online
b2-76.story: Anna's grandpa used to go to the bank every week to pay his bills. This year, Anna decided to teach him how to use [[online banking]] on his phone. Grandma had already tried [[internet banking]] on her laptop, but she found the website confusing. Anna showed them that their card even gave them [[cashback]] on groceries. Grandpa still had questions, so they called his [[account manager]] at the bank. She was very patient, even though she usually works with [[business clients|business client]] like shops and cafes. By the end of the week, Grandpa had paid all his bills alone. He even made his first [[preorder]]: a new fishing book that comes out in May. Now he calls Anna after every payment to tell her how easy it was.

b2-77.title: A new office job
b2-77.story: Max's sister Sofia had wanted to work in the [[IT sector]] for a long time. In March, she went to a job fair at the [[expo center]] and talked to a dozen companies. She had prepared for it by watching a free [[webinar]] about job interviews. One small company liked her [[résumé]], especially the mobile game she had built as a [[side project]]. During the interview, the manager said the team never worked late on weekends, which Sofia saw as a real [[green flag]]. On her first day, she got a laptop, a quiet [[workspace]] near the window, and a bright yellow [[stapler]]. The old [[copier]] broke twice before lunch, but her new colleagues just laughed about it. On Friday, the whole office went bowling for [[team building]], and Sofia won the first game.

b2-78.title: Planning an offline event
b2-78.story: Ira's online book club decided to hold its first [[offline event]] in a cafe in Kyiv. Ira's cousin, who works as a [[copywriter]], offered to help with the invitation. She said that good [[copywriting]] is about short, warm sentences, not fancy words. Lisa, the club's unofficial [[content manager]], planned social media posts for every day that week. Anna's mama knew a [[brand manager]] at a local bakery, and he agreed to bring free cookies. In return, the bakery wanted a little [[publicity]]. So the club hung a large [[banner]] with the bakery's logo above the cafe door. Then a [[PR specialist]] from a publishing house heard about the event and offered to send a young author. Her boss, the [[PR manager]], said it was cheaper than an ad and great for [[PR]]. On Saturday, sixty people came, and the cookies were gone within an hour.

b2-79.title: On the stock market
b2-79.story: Max's economics teacher started a stock market game for the class. Max decided to be a careful [[investor]] and bought shares in three companies. Ira acted as a [[trader]], buying and selling almost every hour. Lisa played the class [[broker]], so everyone had to send their orders through her. Every morning, they checked how the main stock market [[index]] had changed overnight. In one lesson, the teacher explained how a budget [[deficit]] grows when a country spends more than it earns. Some countries, she added, owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars. On Thursday, Ira put all her money into [[bitcoin]], and its price fell sharply that afternoon. She called it a total [[collapse]], although she had only lost imaginary money. On Friday, the teacher did a quick [[audit]] of everyone's accounts and announced that slow, careful Max had won.

b2-80.title: A millionaire's banquet
b2-80.story: Last summer, Anna worked as a waitress at a fancy hotel in Kyiv. One evening, the hotel hosted a [[banquet]] for a local [[millionaire]] who was celebrating his sixtieth birthday. He arrived with a security [[escort]], which made the whole staff nervous. Anna stood at the door and offered every guest a [[welcome drink]]: fresh juice or [[prosecco]]. Later, she carried silver plates of black [[caviar]] around the room. The manager reminded her that every guest was a [[VIP client]], so she had to smile all night. At midnight, the guests moved to the [[lounge bar]], and Anna could finally sit down. The next morning, she found a thank-you note and a big tip from the birthday man himself.
